claims.title: Unverified encryption may expose landing-bucket extracts in transit
claims.description: `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:landing-bucket>list-and-read-files` carries partner extract files containing health and PII data, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If transport protection is absent, an attacker able to observe the landing-network path can intercept extracts as `process:ingest-scheduler` reads `store:landing-bucket`. The captured member names and dates of birth enable targeted privacy attacks and correlation with the normalized records later loaded into `store:claims-warehouse`. This is conditional on the unverified transport-control attribute, not an assertion that the flow is plaintext.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `encryption_in_transit` is unstated on the intra-landing-network flow, so the attacker also needs an on-path foothold. Impact is high because the flow reads a confidential store holding `pii` and `health` data.

mitigations.detail: Configure TLS for `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:landing-bucket>list-and-read-files`, validate the storage endpoint, and record the resulting `encryption_in_transit` posture.

claims.title: Unverified transport may expose Airflow connection strings and partner keys
claims.description: `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:airflow-metadata-database>read-connections` transfers connection strings and partner SFTP keys, while its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the connection is not protected, an on-path attacker intercepts credentials read by `process:ingest-scheduler` from `store:airflow-metadata-database`. The disclosed partner keys enable access to the partner-upload path represented by `flow:entity:insurance-partner>store:landing-bucket>push-daily-extract`; connection strings can also expose additional service access. This is conditional on the unverified protocol and transport encryption.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the internal flow's protocol and transport encryption are unstated and an attacker must obtain an on-path position. Impact is high because `store:airflow-metadata-database` holds `credentials` and `secrets`, which can unlock the partner ingestion path.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the metadata-database connection
mitigations.detail: Set a verified TLS or mTLS transport and explicit authenticated database protocol for `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:airflow-metadata-database>read-connections`.

mitigations.summary: Replace static partner keys with short-lived credentials
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated secret manager and rotate the partner SFTP keys so an intercepted credential has limited lifetime and scope.

claims.title: Unverified cross-zone transform trigger may reveal claim-processing details
claims.description: `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>process:spark-transform-job>trigger-transform` crosses from `boundary:landing-network` to `boundary:warehouse-network`, but its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the cross-zone transport lacks encryption, an attacker observing that path can intercept run requests that name the partner file being processed and correlate them with sensitive extracts handled by `process:spark-transform-job`. This exposes the ingestion schedule and file-level processing metadata that can guide later targeting of `store:landing-bucket` and `store:claims-warehouse`. The threat is conditional on the unverified transport state.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: the flow crosses the landing and warehouse zones and records neither protocol nor transport encryption, though an attacker still needs path access. Impact is medium because the request identifies sensitive-file processing rather than carrying the claim rows themselves, but it exposes operational metadata useful for targeting health-data processing.

mitigations.detail: Use mutually authenticated TLS for `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>process:spark-transform-job>trigger-transform` and ensure run requests contain only opaque job references rather than sensitive file identifiers.

claims.title: Unverified warehouse-load transport may disclose normalized health records
claims.description: `flow:process:spark-transform-job>store:claims-warehouse>load-records` carries normalized claim records with PII and health data, while its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the BigQuery API connection is not transport-protected, an attacker able to observe the warehouse-network path can intercept the records while `process:spark-transform-job` writes them to `store:claims-warehouse`. The attacker gains member-level claims information that can be correlated with the warehouse's direct analyst query path. This is a conditional finding about the unverified transport attribute.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the warehouse-network flow has unstated transport encryption and requires an on-path foothold. Impact is high because it carries normalized records into the confidential `store:claims-warehouse`, which is tagged `pii` and `health`.

mitigations.detail: Require and verify TLS for `flow:process:spark-transform-job>store:claims-warehouse>load-records`, including certificate validation for the warehouse API endpoint.

claims.title: Unverified analyst-query transport may expose warehouse records on the network
claims.description: `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries` returns claim records including member identifiers over a connection whose `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If transport encryption is absent, an attacker on the warehouse-network path can intercept query results between `entity:data-analyst` and `store:claims-warehouse`. The resulting health and identity data can be used to target individuals and can be combined with the analyst's dataset-wide access to reconstruct broad portions of the corpus. This is conditional on the unstated transport protection.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the analyst-to-warehouse path is internal and an attacker needs network observation capability, although encryption is not stated. Impact is high because the confidential warehouse contains `pii` and `health` data and the flow returns member identifiers.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries` and verify that analysts use approved clients that validate the warehouse endpoint.

claims.title: A storage copy could expose all landing-bucket extracts if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` is confidential and holds partner extracts containing PII and health data, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If this unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a bucket export, snapshot, decommissioned media, or other storage-layer copy can read every landed extract without using the scheduler's access path. The disclosure supplies raw member names and dates of birth before transformation and can be correlated with records subsequently loaded into `store:claims-warehouse`. This claim is conditional and does not assert that encryption is absent.

quotes.text: I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown at-rest posture: a copied storage artifact bypasses application authentication, but encryption may be enabled. Impact is high because the confidential store contains health and PII extracts for all partners, and disclosure of raw records is irreversible.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the landing bucket and operational copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the at-rest posture, then require managed-key encryption for `store:landing-bucket`, including exports, snapshots, backups, and replicas, while restricting export permissions.

claims.title: A copy of the Airflow metadata database could reveal partner keys and connection strings
claims.description: `store:airflow-metadata-database` is confidential, contains credentials and secrets, and has unknown `encryption_at_rest`. If the database is unencrypted at rest, an attacker holding a backup, snapshot, database volume, or other storage copy can recover the connection strings and partner SFTP keys without compromising `process:ingest-scheduler`. The recovered keys enable access to the partner-upload path at `flow:entity:insurance-partner>store:landing-bucket>push-daily-extract` and can support further access wherever the connection strings authenticate. This is conditional on the unknown encryption state.

quotes.text: I don't know ... whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `encryption_at_rest` is unstated, while storage copies can be accessed outside the application's authentication path. Impact is high because the confidential database holds `credentials` and `secrets`, including partner keys that unlock further access.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt metadata storage and every copy
mitigations.detail: Confirm and enforce managed-key encryption at rest for `store:airflow-metadata-database`, including backups and snapshots, and tightly limit decrypt and export permissions.

mitigations.summary: Move and rotate stored connection secrets
mitigations.detail: Store connection strings and partner keys in a dedicated secret manager with short-lived issuance where possible, and rotate the static partner keys.

claims.title: A warehouse storage copy could disclose the normalized claims corpus
claims.description: `store:claims-warehouse` is a confidential BigQuery dataset containing normalized claim records, member names, dates of birth, PII, and health data, but its `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If encryption is absent, an attacker obtaining a storage-layer copy, export, snapshot, or backup can read the claims corpus without presenting SSO credentials through `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries`. The loss is corpus-scale disclosure of member-identifying health information. This is explicitly conditional on the unresolved at-rest control.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the warehouse's encryption-at-rest posture is unknown and copied artifacts bypass live query controls. Impact is high because the confidential warehouse holds a corpus of `pii` and `health` records, including member names and dates of birth.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce warehouse encryption at rest
mitigations.detail: Establish the encryption posture for `store:claims-warehouse`; require managed-key encryption and equivalent protection for all exports, snapshots, backups, and replicas.
Limit export and snapshot permissions to separate, narrowly scoped principals and alert on bulk extraction from the warehouse.

claims.title: Code in the scheduler can read every landing-bucket extract through its existing access
claims.description: `process:ingest-scheduler` lists `store:landing-bucket` nightly and reads whatever files are present through `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:landing-bucket>list-and-read-files`; the flow's authentication is unknown. An attacker who gains code execution in the scheduler can use that existing read path to collect every partner extract, including health and PII data, rather than being limited to a single partner folder. The raw data can then be correlated with the normalized records loaded into `store:claims-warehouse`. This finding concerns the scheduler's existing reader authority; encryption at rest would not prevent reads made through an authorized live service.

quotes.text: lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the attacker must first run code in `process:ingest-scheduler`, but the scheduler's authentication to the bucket is unstated and it reads whatever files are present. Impact is high because `store:landing-bucket` is confidential and contains `pii` and `health` extracts across partners.

mitigations.summary: Constrain scheduler reads to the required partner objects
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated scheduler identity with least-privilege, prefix-scoped permissions and enforce partner-origin and folder ownership checks before reads.
Log object reads by the scheduler identity and alert on volume, timing, or prefixes inconsistent with its nightly processing job.

claims.title: Code in the scheduler can recover Airflow-held partner keys and connection strings
claims.description: `process:ingest-scheduler` reads connection strings and partner SFTP keys from `store:airflow-metadata-database` through `flow:process:ingest-scheduler>store:airflow-metadata-database>read-connections`, whose authentication is unknown. An attacker running code in the scheduler can recover these credentials through the service's normal read path. The partner keys enable access to the ingestion route represented by `flow:entity:insurance-partner>store:landing-bucket>push-daily-extract`, while connection strings may enable additional downstream service access. This is separate from the storage-copy threat because database at-rest encryption does not stop a compromised authorized reader.

quotes.text: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because code execution in `process:ingest-scheduler` is a prerequisite, but the scheduler is a named reader and authentication on its metadata-database flow is unknown. Impact is high because the metadata database holds `credentials` and `secrets`, and the partner static key is stated not to be rotated.

mitigations.summary: Remove long-lived keys from the scheduler-readable metadata database
mitigations.detail: Move partner keys and connection strings to a dedicated secret store, issue narrowly scoped short-lived credentials to the scheduler, and rotate all existing static keys.
Grant the scheduler access only to the individual secrets required for the current job and audit every retrieval from the secret-management path.

claims.title: Dataset-wide analyst access discloses member-identifying claims beyond a need-to-know scope
claims.description: An authorized `entity:data-analyst` queries `store:claims-warehouse` through `flow:entity:data-analyst>store:claims-warehouse>run-queries` using SSO, but the stated grant covers the whole dataset, including member-identifying columns. A legitimate analyst acting beyond a particular analytical need can read the warehouse's health and PII records in bulk. The disclosed member identifiers and claim data can be exported or correlated across the dataset, producing corpus-scale privacy harm; the finding is about abuse of the existing dataset-wide grant, not authentication failure.

quotes.text: the grant is dataset-wide — we have not split member-identifying columns out.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because analysts already authenticate with SSO and have a stated dataset-wide grant over `store:claims-warehouse`. Impact is high because the confidential warehouse holds member-identifying `pii` and `health` claim records, allowing bulk disclosure by an authorized principal.

mitigations.summary: Replace the dataset-wide analyst grant with least-privilege access
mitigations.detail: Split member-identifying columns into separately controlled views or datasets, grant analysts only the rows and fields required for their role, and enforce server-side policy controls.

mitigations.summary: Monitor and limit bulk analytical extraction
mitigations.detail: Audit sensitive-column queries and exports, alert on enumeration-shaped access, and apply approved-purpose controls for access to identified health records.
